verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own Enterprise SSO over SAML and OIDC, with IdP user data synchronized into Clerk, and separately documents multi-tenant Organizations. Nothing in the pack shows an SSO connection scoped to a specific customer organization, domain verification, or explicit just-in-time provisioning into an org. missing for 10: per-organization SSO connection binding, verified-domain configuration, explicit JIT provisioning/auto-membership, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can give each customer organization its own SSO connection with verified domains and just-in-time provisioning

citations.quote: Enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) allows users to sign in seamlessly using their Identity Provider (IdP) credentials (e.g.,Azure AD, Okta, or Google Workspace) and have their user data synchronized with Clerk.
Clerk supports multiple protocols for implementing Enterprise SSO, including SAML and OIDC.
Organizations let you group users with Roles and Permissions. This lets you build multi-tenant B2B apps
